facts.text: I have pain in my right wrist.
It has been going on for more than three months.

facts.item: right wrist pain: how it started
facts.text: It started after a minor strain while I was lifting something.

facts.item: right wrist pain: what makes it worse
facts.text: Even small movements of my wrist hurt.

facts.item: right wrist pain: response to treatment
facts.text: The treatment I've had so far hasn't made it better.
At first I was told it was a wrist sprain.
I was given anti-inflammatory painkillers (NSAIDs) for it.
Later I was told it was osteoarthritis.

facts.item: swelling on the palm side of the wrist
facts.text: There's a new soft swelling on the palm side of my right wrist.

facts.item: red, peeling skin over the wrist
facts.text: The skin over it is red and peeling.
Since this started, I've been moving back and forth between Florida and Canada.
I moved to the United States seven years ago.

findings.name: right wrist examination
findings.result: Erythematous, desquamated, fluctuant lesion on the volar right wrist; pain with small arcs of motion.

findings.name: neurovascular examination of the upper limbs
X-ray of the right wrist
findings.result: Diffuse destruction and osteopenia of the proximal and distal carpal rows with scattered cystic changes of the distal radius, ulna, and carpal bones.

findings.name: contrast-enhanced MRI of the right wrist
findings.result: Diffuse T2-weighted enhancement of the carpal bones and a subcutaneous fluid collection communicating with the radiocarpal joint.

gold.reasoning: 1. A neuropathic joint was considered, but imaging ruled out a syrinx — “the MRI of the cervical spine did not show a syrinx.” 2. Pulmonary tuberculosis was considered, but chest imaging was unremarkable — “the chest radiograph was negative for any acute or indolent pulmonary disease.” 3. Non-infectious inflammatory arthropathy was considered, but the presence of purulent fluid made it less likely — “the fluid appeared grossly purulent.” 4. Aggressive bacterial infection was considered, but rapid-onset pathogens were deemed less likely than indolent organisms — “our differential was narrowed to infectious arthropathy of the wrist and carpus likely secondary to an indolent bacteria or fungi.”

x008: The individual inflammatory markers are not named; ESR and CRP are aliases because they are the usual markers.
x002: Only 'hemodynamically stable' is given; no values for blood pressure or heart rate.

source_issues: No culture, stain or histology result is given (s011 lists what was sent but not the results); tuberculosis is the expert diagnosis from the clinical picture (selection note).
Upper-extremity hyperreflexia is not explained in the prompt (the cervical MRI showed no syrinx).
s004 is ambiguous about which treatment failed ('then with primary osteoarthritis without improvement').
notes: Index visit: the re-presentation with continued right wrist pain and new volar fluctuance, leading to admission (s005–s012); s001–s004 are the history before it (earlier diagnoses of sprain and osteoarthritis).

s011: the aspirate was sent for cytology, Gram stain, aerobic, anaerobic, fungal and acid-fast cultures and crystal analysis, but no results are given, so the only finding is the fluid's appearance (x012).
Earlier diagnoses the patient was given (sprain, osteoarthritis) are medical_history facts; they are not the gold diagnosis.

excluded_sentences.reason: Clinician's presumptive diagnosis (septic arthritis) and a therapeutic procedure (open irrigation and debridement) with its operative findings; hospital course after the index visit.
